sources.bowOnDrag: The raft ends in the butts of its logs, a blunt face: a flat-faced body some times as long as it is thick takes about 0.8 head-on (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3)
sources.broadsideDrag: Its side is the side of a round log: a cylinder of her length to twice her draft, which takes about 1.0 (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3: 1.2 across a subcritical flow, 0.82 of it for a cylinder ten times as long as it is thick)

sources.heave: A raft lies flat on the water and rises with the crest
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Seamanship: a breaking wave as high as the craft's beam can roll it over
sources.rollResponse: Logs lashed side by side, 2 m wide, have great form stability: little roll, though every crest washes over
sources.pitchResponse: A flat raft lies on the water and tilts little with the swell

sources.bowOnDrag: A fine bow parts the water with next to no pressure drag at her speeds: her drag ahead is the friction on her wetted surface
sources.broadsideDrag: A hull's side across the flow: a round bottom and its mirror in the surface make a cylinder of her length to twice her draft, which takes about 1.0 (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3: 1.2 across a subcritical flow, 0.82 of it for a cylinder ten times as long as it is thick)
sources.appendage: Her keel beam as the model draws it, 2 m long and 0.25 m deep and wide below the hull. Head-on it is a blunt face, about 0.8 (Hoerner 1965, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 3); abeam a flat plate eight times as long as it is deep, about 1.2 (Hoerner 1965, ch. 3)

sources.heave: Balance: a planked hull of some weight rises with part of the crest
sources.capsizeBreakerMetres: Wolfson Unit capsize trials after the 1979 Fastnet: a breaker of about 55% of a keelboat's length rolls it; the sailboat is about 6 m
sources.rollResponse: Follows the water's slope as it is, vanilla's own roll where no swell is drawn
sources.pitchResponse: Follows the water's slope as it is, vanilla's own pitch where no swell is drawn
